human_frequency.title: Workplace AI use
human_frequency.population: U.S. employees aged 18+ working for organizations

rows.label: At least a few times a year
A few times a week or more

human_frequency.comparison: Q2 minus Q1: +2 percentage points for each measure. Survey readings, not quarterly averages.
human_frequency.limits: Groups overlap: daily users are included in both broader measures. These are self-reports, not measured productivity. Q3 and Q4 readings are not included in this snapshot.
human_frequency.uncertainty: Point estimates; no confidence intervals for these contrasts are included. Differences are not claimed to be statistically significant.
human_frequency.cadence: Review quarterly; add comparable waves as released.

human_reach.title: Generative AI use beyond the workplace
human_reach.population: All U.S. adults aged 18-64 / any purpose
human_reach.comparison: Two-year changes: +16.2 points for any use; +17.7 points for use in the previous week. This is not a quarter-to-quarter comparison.
human_reach.limits: Both endpoints come from the same current tracker summary. Weekly users are included in any use. Different population and wording from Gallup; keep the series separate. An adjacent-quarter comparison has not been verified here.
human_reach.uncertainty: Point estimates; source-specific uncertainty for these contrasts is not available in this snapshot.
human_reach.cadence: Quarterly survey; add each verified wave, preserving the source vintage.

human_barriers.title: Selected major reasons for not using chatbots
human_barriers.population: U.S. adults who say they never use AI chatbots

rows.label: Do not know how to use them

human_barriers.comparison: No comparable earlier-quarter reading is available in this record. Carry this dated baseline until a matching survey is released.
human_barriers.limits: Major reasons only; respondents could name several. These percentages concern non-users, not all adults. The full survey had 5,119 adults; that is not the non-user subgroup size. Four of five reasons are shown.
human_barriers.uncertainty: Subgroup confidence intervals are not supplied in this snapshot.
human_barriers.cadence: Review quarterly; refresh only when a comparable survey appears.

human_benefits.title: Benefits reported by workplace AI users
human_benefits.population: U.S. employees using AI at work at least a few times in the past year
human_benefits.comparison: Newly published in Q4, using Q1 survey data. No matching earlier-quarter benefits comparison has been verified.
human_benefits.limits: Self-assessed benefits among 7,845 AI users; full employee sample 15,482. Benefits overlap. These percentages are shares reporting a benefit, not sizes of productivity gains. Three of four benefits are shown.
human_benefits.uncertainty: Subgroup confidence intervals are not supplied in this snapshot.
human_benefits.cadence: Review quarterly; retain dates and separate perceptions from measured outcomes.

recurring_panels.title: Frequency of use
recurring_panels.rule: Compare identical questions, populations and frequency cutoffs across waves. Publish percentage-point changes. Never stitch the two surveys together.

recurring_panels.title: Barriers to adoption
recurring_panels.rule: Keep non-users as the denominator, major reasons separate from minor reasons, and overlapping responses visible. Missing quarters remain unavailable.

recurring_panels.title: Reported versus measured benefits
recurring_panels.rule: Place self-reports beside relevant independent outcome studies. Preserve tasks, dates, units and methods; no combined productivity score or universal multiplier.
